practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form of the verb to fill in the blank: 'If he ________ harder, he would have passed the exam last week.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a Third Conditional sentence referring to an unreal past event (indicated by 'last week' and 'would have passed'). The 'if' clause must use the Past Perfect tense ('had studied').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence from the options below:
opts: If you will call me, I will come.
If you call me, I will come.
If you call me, I come.
If you would call me, I would come.
practiceQuestions.sol: In a First Conditional sentence, the conditional clause must take the Simple Present tense ('If you call me'), and the main clause takes the simple future ('I will come').

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the error in the tense usage: 'The train left before we reached the station yesterday.'
practiceQuestions.sol: When two past actions are related in time, the earlier action must be in the Past Perfect tense. The train leaving happened first, so it should be 'had left' instead of 'left'.

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank: 'I ________ him since we were children.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Know' is a stative verb and cannot be used in continuous/progressive forms. To show duration since childhood, the Present Perfect tense ('have known') is required.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct sentence structure using inversion:
opts: Had I known the truth, I would not have believed him.
Had I knew the truth, I would not have believed him.
If I had known the truth, I would not believe him.
Would I have known the truth, I had not believed him.
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Had I known' is the correct inverted form of the Third Conditional clause 'If I had known', paired correctly with the past unreal consequence 'would not have believed'.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'By this time next year, she ________ her graduation degree.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The time marker 'By this time next year' denotes a deadline in the future, which requires the Future Perfect tense ('will have completed').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct verb form: 'Our teacher said that the sun ________ in the east.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Universal truths and scientific facts must be kept in the Simple Present tense, even if the principal reporting verb ('said') is in the past tense.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'If I ________ a king, I would help the poor.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a Second Conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical/unreal present condition. The past subjunctive 'were' must be used for all subjects.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct structure for the sentence: 'Hardly ________ entered the room when the lights went out.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Hardly' is a negative adverb that requires subject-auxiliary inversion when placed at the beginning of a clause. Thus, 'had he' is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct sentence from the options:
opts: We have been living here since 2015.
practiceQuestions.sol: An action that began in the past and is still continuing up to the present requires the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('have been living') with the point in time marker 'since'.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She ________ to the market before I called her.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The action of going to the market took place before another past action (calling). Therefore, the earlier action must be in the Past Perfect ('had gone').

practiceQuestions.q: What is the correct conditional structure: 'If he ________ rich, he would buy a yacht.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This represents a Second Conditional (hypothetical present/future state). The subjunctive form 'were' is used in the 'if' clause.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct verb form: 'I ________ a book when he knocked at the door.'
practiceQuestions.sol: A continuous background action in the past ('was reading') was interrupted by a short completed action ('knocked'). Hence, Past Continuous is appropriate.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct inversion structure: '________ you need any help, do not hesitate to contact me.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Should you need' is the correct inverted form of the First Conditional 'If you should need'.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'Since she started her new job, she ________ extremely busy.'
practiceQuestions.sol: An action or state that started in the past and has continued to the present is expressed in the Present Perfect ('has been').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If he had run fast, he would catch the train.
If he ran fast, he would have caught the train.
If he had run fast, he would have caught the train.
If he would have run fast, he would catch the train.
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a standard Third Conditional structure: If + Past Perfect ('had run'), would have + V3 ('would have caught').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'I ________ for the exam for three hours before my friend arrived.'
practiceQuestions.sol: An action that was in progress for a duration ('for three hours') before another past point ('friend arrived') must be in the Past Perfect Continuous ('had been studying').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct option: 'Water ________ at 0 degrees Celsius.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Universal scientific facts are always expressed in the Simple Present tense ('freezes').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He behaves as if he ________ everything.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The phrase 'as if' introduces an unreal/imaginary comparison. Thus, it requires the past subjunctive form ('knew') to denote present unreality.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the correct structure: 'No sooner ________ the station than the train left.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'No sooner' at the beginning of a sentence requires inversion of the auxiliary verb. 'had we reached' is correct, followed by 'than' for the main clause.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'It is high time we ________ studying seriously.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The phrases 'It is high time' or 'It is time' are followed by the subjunctive Simple Past (V2) to express a present necessity that is overdue.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He ________ to London last month.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Last month' is a definite past time marker, which requires the Simple Past tense ('traveled').

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct option: 'When I reach home, my mother ________ food.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This expresses a future action in progress at a specific time in the future, which is denoted by the Future Continuous ('will be cooking').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct conditional structure: 'Were she my daughter, I ________ not allow her to go out late.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Were she my daughter' is the inverted form of the Second Conditional 'If she were my daughter'. The main clause requires 'would + V1'.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'I ________ my dinner before my brother returned.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The finishing of dinner occurred before another past event (brother's return). Therefore, the earlier past action must be in the Past Perfect ('had finished').

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct sentence:
opts: Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
If you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you will work hard, you will fail.
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Unless' is negative in meaning (meaning 'if not'). It should not be followed by 'not'. Also, it cannot take 'will' in its clause.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'If he ________ to me, I would have helped him.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a Third Conditional sentence ('would have helped'). The conditional clause must use the Past Perfect ('had come').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He ________ in this company for five years.'
practiceQuestions.sol: An action showing continuation and duration ('for five years') from the past to the present requires the Present Perfect Continuous ('has been working').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: I will write to you when I will arrive.
I will write to you when I arrive.
I write to you when I will arrive.
I will write to you when I would arrive.
practiceQuestions.sol: In clauses introduced by time connectors like *when, before, after, until*, do not use the future tense. Use the Simple Present ('when I arrive') instead.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'If I had not lost my passport, I ________ on a plane right now.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a mixed conditional: an unreal past condition ('had not lost') with a present continuing result ('right now'). Hence, 'would be flying' is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct option: 'By the end of this month, we ________ here for two years.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'By the end of this month' coupled with a duration ('for two years') requires the Future Perfect Continuous tense ('will have been living').

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct sentence using 'lest':
opts: Walk carefully lest you should not fall.
Walk carefully lest you should fall.
Walk carefully lest you will fall.
Walk carefully lest you would fall.
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Lest' is inherently negative and must be paired with 'should' without the negative word 'not'.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'I ________ a sound sleep last night.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Last night' is a definite past time marker, requiring the Simple Past tense ('had').

practiceQuestions.q: What is the correct structure: 'If they ________ more time, they could have finished the project.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a Third Conditional sentence. The past perfect of the verb 'have' is 'had had' (auxiliary 'had' + V3 'had').

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct option: 'I wish I ________ rich.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Present imaginary wishes use the past subjunctive form 'were' for all subjects.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'The bell ________ before I reached school.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The ringing of the bell occurred before reaching school, requiring Past Perfect ('had rung') for the earlier past action.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: We are knowing each other for a long time.
We know each other for a long time.
We have known each other for a long time.
We have been knowing each other for a long time.
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Know' is a stative verb. Duration must be expressed in the Present Perfect ('have known').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She ________ her homework before she went to bed.'
practiceQuestions.sol: The finishing of homework was completed before going to bed, requiring Past Perfect ('had finished') for the earlier past action.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct option: 'If he ________ now, he will miss the train.'
practiceQuestions.sol: This is a First Conditional sentence. The conditional clause takes the Simple Present negative ('does not leave').

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct form: 'Since the accident, he ________ afraid of driving.'
practiceQuestions.sol: A state that started in the past (at the accident) and continues to the present requires the Present Perfect ('has been').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'I ________ him yesterday.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Definite past time markers like 'yesterday' require Simple Past ('met').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If I had known, I would tell you.
If I knew, I would have told you.
If I had known, I would have told you.
If I would have known, I would have told you.
practiceQuestions.sol: Standard Third Conditional: If + Past Perfect ('had known'), would have + V3 ('would have told').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'He ________ since morning.'
practiceQuestions.sol: An action continuing from past to present starting at a specific point ('since morning') takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been reading').

practiceQuestions.q: What is the correct structure: 'If he ________ harder, he would have succeeded.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Third Conditional: If + Past Perfect ('had tried'), would have + V3.

practiceQuestions.q: Select the correct option: 'It ________ since yesterday.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Action continuing from a point in the past to present takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been raining').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'The train ________ before I reached the station.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Past Perfect ('had left') is required for the earlier of the two past actions.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: I have seen him last week.
I had seen him last week.
I have been seeing him last week.
practiceQuestions.sol: Definite past time reference ('last week') requires Simple Past ('saw').

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'If you ________ the truth, you would not be in trouble now.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Mixed conditional: past unreal action ('had spoken') with present result ('would not be in trouble now').

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the correct option: 'He ________ writing stories for ten years.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Duration from past to present takes Present Perfect Continuous ('has been' + writing).

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'Should she ________, tell her I am waiting.'
practiceQuestions.sol: After inverted 'Should', use the base form of the verb ('come') without '-s'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the correct form of the verb: 'If I ________ a bird, I would fly in the sky.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: This is a Second Conditional (hypothetical present). Use subjunctive 'were' for all subjects.

opts: Unless you do not hurry, you will miss the train.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.
If you hurry, you will miss the train.
Unless you will hurry, you will miss the train.
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Unless' is negative and cannot take 'not' or 'will' in its clause.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the error in tense: 'By the time the doctor had arrived, the patient died.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: The patient dying happened first, so it should be 'had died' (Past Perfect), and the doctor arriving happened second, so it should be 'arrived' (Simple Past). Thus, 'had arrived' is the error.

mockTestQuestions.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank: 'I ________ this house since 2018.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Own' is a stative verb of possession, which does not take continuous aspect. Use Present Perfect 'have owned'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the correct sentence structure using inversion:
opts: Had we played well, we would have won.
Had we played well, we had won.
If we had played well, we would win.
Would we have played well, we had won.
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Had we played well' is the correct inverted Third Conditional clause, matched with 'would have won'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'By next December, we ________ here for five years.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'By next December' paired with a duration ('for five years') requires Future Perfect Continuous 'will have been living'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Choose the correct verb form: 'Water ________ at 100 degrees Celsius.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Scientific facts are expressed in Simple Present 'boils'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'If he ________ earlier, he would have met the director.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Third Conditional past unreal: If + Past Perfect ('had arrived'), would have + V3.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the correct structure: 'No sooner ________ seen the police than he ran away.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Inversion is required after 'No sooner' at the start of a sentence: 'had he' is correct.

mockTestQuestions.q: Choose the correct sentence from the options:
opts: It has been raining since morning.
mockTestQuestions.sol: Action continuing from a past point to the present requires Present Perfect Continuous 'has been raining'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She ________ the office before I arrived.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Earlier of two past actions requires Past Perfect ('had left').

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the correct conditional structure: 'Were he to ask me, I ________ help him.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Inverted Second Conditional 'Were he to ask me' requires 'would + V1' in the main clause.

mockTestQuestions.q: Choose the correct verb form: 'He ________ TV when the door bell rang.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: Background continuous past action ('was watching') interrupted by a short completed action ('rang').

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the correct inversion structure: '________ you fail to comply, penalties will apply.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Should you fail' is the inverted First Conditional 'If you should fail'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the correct form: 'Since she changed schools, she ________ much happier.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: State starting at a past point and continuing to the present requires Present Perfect 'has been'.
